critical_code_review_comments: useUserLayout hook (DraggableTiles.jsx) is well-designed: reconciles stale ids on each load, debounces PUT by 400ms, mirrors to localStorage as fast-path cache, gracefully degrades on network errors. Good defensive coding.

Backend layout endpoints (server.py:2384-2416) correctly upsert by (user_id, page_key) compound key, enforce 1≤len(order)≤200, and exclude _id in response. RBAC is appropriately permissive (any authenticated user) — layouts are user-scoped via session, so no over-share risk.

Inconsistency: Dashboard.jsx wires useUserLayout('dashboard') but does NOT use the universal DraggableTiles wrapper — it has its own dragHandle component. This means the universal tile-{pageKey}-{id} and drag-{pageKey}-{id} testids the review request expected are absent on Dashboard. Functionality still works (server persistence + reset confirmed), only the testid convention diverges.
MiniCalendar uses internal-only state — no backend events feed into it. The component spec called this out explicitly ('No backend hookup yet'). It is purely visual.
